Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the deep dive with you and Michael. Quick recap and a few asks so we can move the procurement/commercial path forward:

- Use case: inference for customer-facing product (batch + streaming).
- Expected spend: pilot ~$10k/mo ramping to ~$50k/mo within 3–6 months.
- Technical follow-ups: endpoint SLA and SOC 2 evidence (we'll send links separately).

2) Procurement / commercial questions (please confirm):
- Preferred payment method: PO vs corporate card?
- Net terms typically expected (Net 30 / Net 45 / prepaid)?
- Invoice requirements: invoice name, legal entity, billing address, tax/VAT ID, preferred invoice format (PDF / XML / XLSX).
- Marketplace interest: would you prefer to purchase via AWS Marketplace or directly with Redwood (affects billing flow)?

3) Next steps from our side:
- I can send a draft SOW and sample invoice template for your billing team to confirm format.
- If you prefer PO, please confirm the procurement contact and any vendor forms (W-9, supplier onboarding) we should complete.

If you can reply with your procurement contact and an indication of PO vs card and net terms, I’ll attach the SOW + invoice template and route to our billing ops for any additional info.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Dylan and Dev to help with technical/contract questions as needed.

Hi Marissa —

Great summary, thank you. A few notes from procurement/legal side: 

- Payment method: For deals of this size our preferred flow is a Purchase Order (PO) and ACH payment. We rarely use corporate card for enterprise commitments.
- Net terms: Standard is Net 30 for preferred vendors; exceptions require finance approval.
- Invoice details: Invoice must be addressed to "Acme Corp" (legal: Acme Corporation), include our Tax ID: 12-3456789, and the billing address: 100 Market St, Suite 200, San Francisco, CA 94105.
- Invoice format: PDF is fine; we also accept an XLSX sample if it helps automate ingestion.
- Vendor forms: I’m attaching our vendor onboarding packet (W-9 + procurement checklist). Please complete and return.
- PO issuance: I will start the PO request once we have a final SOW and the vendor onboarding info. PO typically takes 7–10 business days to get approved.
- Marketplace: We prefer direct procurement for now; marketplace billing complicates tax handling for us.

CC'ing Michael for legal if he needs to review any contract language.

Thanks — once you send SOW + invoice template and the vendor W-9 completed, I’ll route for PO.

Best,
Elena Garcia
Director, Procurement
